questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is weathering?

options.A: The removal and transportation of rock material by rivers and wind
options.B: The in-situ disintegration, decomposition or alteration of rocks and minerals at or near Earth's surface
options.C: The downslope movement of rock or soil under gravity
options.D: The deposition of sediments in river valleys

questions.explanation: Weathering is the in-situ disintegration, decomposition or alteration of rocks and minerals at or near Earth's surface by physical, chemical and biological processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is weathering called an in-situ process?

options.A: Because the material is transported far from its origin
options.B: Because rock is broken down or chemically altered where it is located

questions.explanation: Weathering is called in-situ because rock is broken down or chemically altered where it is located; the material generally remains at or near its place of origin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between weathering and erosion?

options.A: Weathering removes material; erosion breaks it in place
options.B: Weathering breaks down rock in place; erosion removes and transports material
options.D: Erosion is in-situ; weathering involves transport

questions.explanation: Weathering breaks down rock in place, while erosion involves removal and transportation of weathered material by rivers, wind, glaciers, waves or other agents.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is mass wasting?

options.A: Chemical alteration of rock in place
options.B: Downslope movement of rock or soil under gravity
options.D: Freezing and thawing of water in rock cracks

questions.explanation: Mass wasting is the downslope movement of rock or soil under gravity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is regolith?

options.B: The loose, unconsolidated layer of weathered rock and mineral material covering bedrock
options.C: A type of chemical weathering process
options.D: Molten rock beneath the Earth's surface

questions.explanation: Regolith is the loose, unconsolidated layer of weathered rock and mineral material covering bedrock.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is soil in relation to regolith?

options.A: Soil is completely unrelated to regolith
options.B: Soil is a biologically active part of regolith containing mineral particles, organic matter, water and air
options.C: Soil is the same as bedrock
options.D: Soil is a type of mass wasting

questions.explanation: Soil is a biologically active part of regolith containing mineral particles, organic matter, water and air.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Does weathering always produce soil?

options.B: No, weathering supplies mineral material but soil development also depends on climate, organisms, relief, parent material and time
options.C: Yes, but only in tropical regions
options.D: No, weathering never contributes to soil formation

questions.explanation: Weathering supplies mineral material, but soil development also depends on climate, organisms, relief, parent material and time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the three broad types of weathering?
questions.explanation: The three broad types are physical (mechanical), chemical and biological weathering. They often operate together rather than independently.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is physical weathering?

options.A: Decomposition of rock through chemical reactions
options.B: Breakdown of rock into smaller fragments without significant change in chemical or mineral composition
options.C: Alteration of rock by living organisms
options.D: Transport of rock fragments by wind

questions.explanation: Physical weathering is the breakdown of rock into smaller fragments without significant change in chemical or mineral composition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What effect does physical weathering have on chemical weathering?

options.A: It slows down chemical weathering by reducing surface area
options.B: It increases exposed surface area and can accelerate chemical weathering
options.D: It has no effect on chemical weathering

questions.explanation: Physical weathering increases exposed surface area and can accelerate chemical weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main mechanisms of physical weathering?

options.B: Thermal expansion and contraction; frost action; pressure release and unloading; salt-crystal growth; wetting and drying; and mechanical abrasion
options.D: Root wedging and organic acid dissolution

questions.explanation: The main mechanisms of physical weathering are thermal expansion and contraction; frost action (freeze-thaw); pressure release and unloading; salt-crystal growth; wetting and drying; and mechanical abrasion. Exfoliation is a characteristic sheet-peeling effect.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does thermal weathering occur?

options.B: Repeated heating and cooling cause expansion and contraction; differential expansion among minerals creates stress, cracks and granular disintegration
options.C: Through the freezing of water in cracks
options.D: Through the growth of salt crystals in pores

questions.explanation: Thermal weathering occurs through repeated heating and cooling causing expansion and contraction. Differential expansion among minerals creates stress, cracks and granular disintegration. It can be important where daily temperature ranges are large.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is exfoliation?

options.A: The dissolving of calcite in acidic water
options.B: Peeling or separation of curved, concentric outer sheets or slabs from a rock mass, often resembling onion layers
options.C: The freezing and expansion of water in rock cracks
options.D: The chemical combination of water with a mineral

questions.explanation: Exfoliation is the peeling or separation of curved, concentric outer sheets or slabs from a rock mass, often resembling onion layers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Explain exfoliation by pressure release (unloading).

options.A: When overlying material is removed, pressure on formerly buried massive rock decreases; the rock expands slightly and sheet joints develop roughly parallel to the land surface; outer slabs may detach
options.B: Water freezes in cracks and expands by 9%
options.C: Saline water enters pores and evaporates
options.D: Iron-bearing minerals oxidise to iron oxides

questions.explanation: When overlying material is removed, pressure on formerly buried massive rock decreases. The rock expands slightly and sheet joints develop roughly parallel to the land surface; outer slabs may detach.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Is exfoliation caused only by heating and cooling?

options.A: Yes, thermal expansion is the only cause
options.B: No, pressure release and sheet-joint development are important explanations; the dominant mechanism varies with rock and setting
options.C: Yes, exfoliation is exclusively a chemical process
options.D: No, exfoliation is caused only by frost action

questions.explanation: Textbooks sometimes emphasise thermal expansion, but pressure release and sheet-joint development are important explanations. The dominant mechanism varies with rock and setting.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is frost action?

options.A: Water enters joints and cracks; on freezing it expands by about 9% in volume, exerting pressure on crack walls; repeated freeze-thaw cycles widen cracks and detach angular fragments
options.B: Saline water enters pores and crystallises
options.C: Iron minerals oxidise and weaken rock

questions.explanation: Frost action: water enters joints and cracks. On freezing it expands by about 9% in volume, exerting pressure on crack walls. Repeated freeze-thaw cycles widen cracks and detach angular fragments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where is frost action most effective?

options.B: Where temperatures repeatedly cross the freezing point and water is available, particularly high mountains and cold regions
options.D: In coastal areas with high salinity

questions.explanation: Frost action is most effective where temperatures repeatedly cross the freezing point and water is available, particularly high mountains and cold regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is salt weathering?

options.A: Saline water enters pores and cracks; crystal growth, crystallisation cycles or salt hydration exert pressure and disaggregate rock
options.B: Water freezes in cracks and expands
options.C: Iron minerals oxidise to form rust

questions.explanation: Salt weathering: saline water enters pores and cracks; crystal growth, crystallisation cycles or salt hydration exert pressure and disaggregate rock. It is common in arid and coastal settings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which environments is salt weathering common?
questions.explanation: Salt weathering is common in arid and coastal settings where saline water enters pores and evaporates.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do wetting and drying cause weathering?

options.A: Some clay-rich materials swell when wet and shrink when dry; repeated cycles create stress, cracks and weakening
options.B: Water freezes and expands in cracks

questions.explanation: Some clay-rich materials swell when wet and shrink when dry. Repeated cycles create stress, cracks and weakening.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is chemical weathering?

options.A: Breakdown of rock into smaller fragments without chemical change
options.B: Decomposition or alteration of rocks and minerals through reactions with water, dissolved substances, oxygen and atmospheric gases
options.C: Physical breaking of rock by plant roots
options.D: Transport of weathered material by rivers

questions.explanation: Chemical weathering is the decomposition or alteration of rocks and minerals through reactions with water, dissolved substances, oxygen and atmospheric gases. It changes mineral composition and may form new minerals such as clay.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which conditions favour chemical weathering?

options.B: Warmth, moisture, water circulation, reactive minerals, vegetation and a large exposed surface area

questions.explanation: Warmth, moisture, water circulation, reactive minerals, vegetation and a large exposed surface area generally accelerate chemical weathering. Rates also depend on drainage, acidity and rock composition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Name the principal chemical weathering processes.

options.A: Frost action, exfoliation and salt weathering
options.B: Solution, carbonation, oxidation, hydration and hydrolysis
options.C: Root wedging, abrasion and thermal expansion

questions.explanation: The principal chemical weathering processes are solution, carbonation, oxidation, hydration and hydrolysis. Some school classifications also include reduction and chelation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is solution (dissolution) in weathering?

options.A: Direct dissolving of soluble minerals in water
options.C: Chemical combination of water with a mineral
options.D: Reaction of water with minerals changing their composition

questions.explanation: Solution (dissolution) is the direct dissolving of soluble minerals in water. Halite and gypsum are examples; calcite can dissolve in acidic water, particularly water containing carbonic acid.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which minerals are examples of substances that dissolve directly in water?
questions.explanation: Halite and gypsum are examples of soluble minerals that dissolve directly in water. Calcite can dissolve in acidic water, particularly water containing carbonic acid.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is carbonation?

options.A: Carbon dioxide dissolves in water to form weak carbonic acid; this reacts with carbonate minerals, especially calcite in limestone, producing soluble calcium bicarbonate that is carried away in groundwater
options.B: Iron-bearing minerals oxidise to iron oxides
options.C: Water combines chemically with a mineral structure
options.D: Minerals react with water and form clay

questions.explanation: Carbonation: carbon dioxide dissolves in water to form weak carbonic acid. This reacts with carbonate minerals, especially calcite in limestone, producing soluble calcium bicarbonate that is carried away in groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What landforms are associated with carbonation?

options.B: Karst features: enlarged joints and grikes, sinkholes/dolines, swallow holes, caves, caverns and underground drainage

questions.explanation: Landforms associated with carbonation include karst features: enlarged joints and grikes, sinkholes/dolines, swallow holes, caves, caverns and underground drainage. Stalactites and stalagmites form later by precipitation of calcium carbonate from dripping water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do stalactites and stalagmites form?

options.A: By freezing of water in caves
options.B: By precipitation of calcium carbonate from dripping water after dissolution and transport

questions.explanation: Stalactites and stalagmites form by precipitation of calcium carbonate from dripping water after dissolution and transport.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is oxidation in weathering?

options.A: A reaction involving oxygen/electron transfer; iron-bearing minerals commonly oxidise to iron oxides and hydroxides, producing red, yellow or brown staining and weakening rock
options.B: Direct dissolving of minerals in water
options.C: Chemical combination of water with a mineral
options.D: Reaction of water with minerals to form clay

questions.explanation: Oxidation is a reaction involving oxygen/electron transfer. Iron-bearing minerals commonly oxidise to iron oxides and hydroxides, producing red, yellow or brown staining and weakening rock.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Give examples of oxidation products in weathering.
questions.explanation: Iron-bearing minerals may weather to hematite and goethite, which commonly impart red, yellow or brown colours.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is hydration in weathering?

options.A: Chemical combination of water molecules with a mineral, often changing its structure and volume
options.B: Direct dissolving of minerals in water
options.D: Reaction of water with minerals changing their composition

questions.explanation: Hydration is the chemical combination of water molecules with a mineral, often changing its structure and volume. An example is anhydrite (CaSO4) hydrating to gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an example of hydration?
questions.explanation: Anhydrite (CaSO4) hydrating to gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) is an example of hydration, which incorporates water into a mineral structure.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Differentiate hydration and hydrolysis.

options.A: Hydration incorporates water into a mineral structure; hydrolysis involves reaction of water (often H+ or OH-) with a mineral, changing its composition
options.B: Hydration involves oxygen; hydrolysis involves carbon dioxide
options.C: Hydration dissolves minerals; hydrolysis freezes water

questions.explanation: Hydration incorporates water into a mineral structure. Hydrolysis involves reaction of water (often H+ or OH-) with a mineral, changing its composition; feldspar can alter to clay minerals.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is hydrolysis?

options.A: Reaction between minerals and water in which ions are exchanged or removed and new minerals form
options.B: Direct dissolving of minerals in water
options.C: Chemical combination of water with a mineral structure

questions.explanation: Hydrolysis is a reaction between minerals and water in which ions are exchanged or removed and new minerals form. Feldspar may be transformed into kaolinite or other clay minerals, releasing dissolved ions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Feldspar commonly alters to clay minerals through which process?
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis changes feldspar composition and can form clay minerals such as kaolinite.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is carbonation important in limestone regions?

options.A: Limestone is rich in quartz which dissolves easily
options.B: Limestone is rich in calcite, which reacts with weak carbonic acid; dissolution along joints creates underground drainage and karst topography
options.C: Limestone contains iron which oxidises rapidly
options.D: Limestone is resistant to all chemical weathering

questions.explanation: Limestone is rich in calcite, which reacts with weak carbonic acid. Dissolution along joints creates underground drainage and karst topography.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is biological weathering?

options.A: Physical breakdown or chemical alteration of rock caused by living organisms and their activities
options.B: Breakdown of rock by temperature changes
options.C: Dissolution of rock by carbonic acid
options.D: Transport of weathered material by organisms

questions.explanation: Biological weathering is the physical breakdown or chemical alteration of rock caused by living organisms and their activities.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do plants cause weathering?

options.A: Roots enter cracks and grow, exerting pressure that widens them; roots and decaying plant matter can also release organic acids that promote chemical alteration
options.B: Plants absorb all water from rocks
options.C: Plants prevent any weathering from occurring

questions.explanation: Roots enter cracks and grow, exerting pressure that widens them. Roots and decaying plant matter can also release organic acids that promote chemical alteration.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do lichens and microorganisms weather rocks?

options.B: They retain moisture and may release organic acids or other compounds that dissolve or alter minerals; they can help initiate soil formation
options.C: They prevent weathering by covering the rock surface
options.D: They only grow on already weathered rock

questions.explanation: Lichens, bacteria and fungi retain moisture and may release organic acids or other compounds that dissolve or alter minerals. They can help initiate soil formation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do animals and humans contribute to weathering?

options.A: Burrowing animals disturb and expose material; human excavation, quarrying, mining, construction, ploughing and vegetation removal expose fresh rock or alter soil and water contact
options.B: They have no effect on weathering
options.D: They prevent weathering by stabilising rock

questions.explanation: Burrowing animals disturb and expose material. Human excavation, quarrying, mining, construction, ploughing and vegetation removal expose fresh rock or alter soil and water contact.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Is biological weathering only physical?

options.A: Yes, biological weathering is always mechanical
options.B: No, root wedging is mechanical while organic-acid reactions and microbial alteration are chemical; biological weathering includes both
options.C: Yes, biological weathering is always chemical
options.D: No, biological weathering never involves chemical processes

questions.explanation: Biological weathering includes both mechanical processes (such as root wedging) and chemical processes (such as organic-acid reactions and microbial alteration).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main controlling factors of weathering?

options.A: Climate; rock/mineral composition; rock structure; surface area; relief and drainage; vegetation and organisms; and time

questions.explanation: The main controlling factors are climate; rock/mineral composition; rock structure; surface area; relief and drainage; vegetation and organisms; and time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does rock/mineral composition control weathering?

options.A: Minerals differ in resistance; quartz is relatively resistant to chemical weathering; many feldspars and ferromagnesian minerals alter more readily; calcite is susceptible to weakly acidic water; texture and cementation also matter
options.B: All minerals weather at the same rate
options.D: Composition has no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Minerals differ in resistance. Quartz is relatively resistant to chemical weathering; many feldspars and ferromagnesian minerals alter more readily; calcite is susceptible to weakly acidic water. Texture and cementation also matter.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does rock structure control weathering?

options.A: Joints, bedding planes, faults, fractures and cleavage provide pathways for water, air and roots; closely jointed rocks expose more surfaces to weathering
options.B: Rock structure has no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Joints, bedding planes, faults, fractures and cleavage provide pathways for water, air and roots. Closely jointed rocks expose more surfaces to weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does surface area affect weathering?

options.A: Small fragments have a larger surface-area-to-volume ratio than one large block of equal mass and generally weather faster
options.B: Surface area has no effect on weathering
options.C: Larger blocks weather faster than small fragments
options.D: Surface area only affects chemical weathering

questions.explanation: Small fragments have a larger surface-area-to-volume ratio than one large block of equal mass and generally weather faster.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do relief, slope and drainage affect weathering?

options.A: Slope affects water residence time, runoff and removal of weathered material; drainage controls the circulation of fresh water and oxygen and the chemical conditions within rock and soil
options.B: Relief and drainage have no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Slope affects water residence time, runoff and removal of weathered material. Drainage controls the circulation of fresh water and oxygen and the chemical conditions within rock and soil.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does vegetation and organisms affect weathering?

options.A: Roots, soil organisms, organic acids and decaying litter influence moisture, acidity and mechanical stress; vegetation may protect the surface while promoting weathering below it
options.B: Vegetation has no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Roots, soil organisms, organic acids and decaying litter influence moisture, acidity and mechanical stress. Vegetation may protect the surface while promoting weathering below it.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does time affect weathering?

options.A: Longer exposure generally allows more weathering if conditions remain favourable and material is not removed; age alone does not determine the degree of weathering
options.B: Time has no effect on weathering
options.D: Age alone determines the degree of weathering

questions.explanation: Longer exposure generally allows more weathering if conditions remain favourable and material is not removed. Age alone does not determine the degree of weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why does a warm, humid climate favour chemical weathering?

options.A: Water supports dissolution and chemical reactions, while higher temperatures generally accelerate reaction rates; soil CO2 and organic acids can further increase the chemical activity of water
options.C: Chemical weathering only occurs in cold climates

questions.explanation: Water supports dissolution and chemical reactions, while higher temperatures generally accelerate reaction rates. Soil CO2 and organic acids can further increase the chemical activity of water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why can the same rock weather differently in different climates?

options.A: Water availability, temperature range, freeze-thaw frequency, vegetation, drainage and exposure differ, changing both the dominant process and its rate
options.D: Climate has no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Water availability, temperature range, freeze-thaw frequency, vegetation, drainage and exposure differ, changing both the dominant process and its rate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main effect of physical weathering?

options.C: Organisms cause physical and/or chemical change

questions.explanation: The main effect of physical weathering is breaking rock into fragments. There is little or no chemical change in composition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main effect of chemical weathering?
questions.explanation: The main effect of chemical weathering is changing mineral composition. It may form new minerals such as clay.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main effect of biological weathering?

options.C: Organisms cause physical and/or chemical change

questions.explanation: Biological weathering involves organisms causing physical and/or chemical change. It may or may not change composition.

questions.explanation: The agents of physical weathering are temperature, ice, salts and pressure.

questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide dissolves in water to form weak carbonic acid, which reacts with calcite in limestone producing soluble calcium bicarbonate Ca(HCO3)2 that is carried away in groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are grikes in karst topography?

options.A: Enlarged joints formed by carbonation dissolution

questions.explanation: Grikes are enlarged joints formed by carbonation dissolution in limestone terrains, part of karst features.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are dolines?
questions.explanation: Dolines are sinkholes formed by limestone dissolution, a karst feature associated with carbonation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are swallow holes?

options.A: Points where surface water disappears underground in karst regions

questions.explanation: Swallow holes are points where surface water disappears underground in karst regions, associated with carbonation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a cavern in karst topography?

options.A: A large underground cave formed by limestone dissolution

questions.explanation: Caverns are large underground caves formed by limestone dissolution, a karst feature associated with carbonation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which world examples are cited for karst topography?

options.A: Dinaric Karst and Guilin region of China

questions.explanation: World examples of karst include the Dinaric Karst and Guilin region of China.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process is a particular acid-assisted reaction involving CO2 and water?
questions.explanation: Carbonation is a particular acid-assisted reaction involving CO2 and water, distinct from direct solution.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process involves reaction of water (often H+ or OH-) with a mineral, changing its composition?
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis involves reaction of water (often H+ or OH-) with a mineral, changing its composition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process incorporates water into a mineral structure?
questions.explanation: Hydration incorporates water into a mineral structure, often changing its structure and volume.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process involves a reaction with oxygen/electron transfer?
questions.explanation: Oxidation is a reaction involving oxygen/electron transfer.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two iron oxides commonly impart red, yellow or brown colours to weathered rock?
questions.explanation: Iron-bearing minerals may weather to hematite and goethite, which commonly impart red, yellow or brown colours.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Anhydrite hydrates to gypsum. What is the chemical formula of gypsum?
questions.explanation: Gypsum is CaSO4·2H2O, formed by hydration of anhydrite (CaSO4).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the chemical formula of anhydrite?
questions.explanation: Anhydrite is CaSO4; it hydrates to gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Feldspar may be transformed into which mineral through hydrolysis?
questions.explanation: Feldspar may be transformed into kaolinite or other clay minerals through hydrolysis, releasing dissolved ions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which minerals are susceptible to weakly acidic water?
questions.explanation: Calcite is susceptible to weakly acidic water, which is why carbonation is important in limestone regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which minerals alter more readily than quartz?
questions.explanation: Many feldspars and ferromagnesian minerals alter more readily than quartz.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What provides pathways for water, air and roots in rock?

options.A: Joints, bedding planes, faults, fractures and cleavage

questions.explanation: Joints, bedding planes, faults, fractures and cleavage provide pathways for water, air and roots.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Closely jointed rocks expose more surfaces to weathering, which means:

options.C: They do not weather at all

questions.explanation: Closely jointed rocks expose more surfaces to weathering, so they weather more rapidly.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Small fragments have a larger surface-area-to-volume ratio than one large block of equal mass and generally:
questions.explanation: Small fragments have a larger surface-area-to-volume ratio and generally weather faster.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Slope affects water residence time, runoff and:
questions.explanation: Slope affects water residence time, runoff and removal of weathered material.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Drainage controls the circulation of fresh water and oxygen and the:

questions.explanation: Drainage controls the circulation of fresh water and oxygen and the chemical conditions within rock and soil.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Vegetation may protect the surface while:
questions.explanation: Vegetation may protect the surface while promoting weathering below it.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Longer exposure generally allows more weathering if:

options.A: Conditions remain favourable and material is not removed

questions.explanation: Longer exposure generally allows more weathering if conditions remain favourable and material is not removed. Age alone does not determine the degree of weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Soil CO2 and organic acids can further increase the:
questions.explanation: Soil CO2 and organic acids can further increase the chemical activity of water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What changes both the dominant process and its rate in the same rock across climates?

options.A: Water availability, temperature range, freeze-thaw frequency, vegetation, drainage and exposure

questions.explanation: Water availability, temperature range, freeze-thaw frequency, vegetation, drainage and exposure differ across climates, changing both the dominant process and its rate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a physical weathering process?
questions.explanation: Mechanical abrasion is a physical weathering mechanism, along with thermal expansion, frost action, pressure release, salt-crystal growth and wetting/drying.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process causes granular disintegration through differential expansion among minerals?
questions.explanation: Thermal weathering: differential expansion among minerals creates stress, cracks and granular disintegration.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Sheet joints develop roughly parallel to the land surface due to:
questions.explanation: When overlying material is removed, pressure decreases, rock expands slightly, and sheet joints develop roughly parallel to the land surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Exfoliation domes occur in which type of landscape?
questions.explanation: Exfoliation domes occur in granitic landscapes worldwide, including parts of the Indian Peninsular uplands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Salt crystallisation in rock pores is common in:
questions.explanation: Salt weathering (crystal growth, crystallisation cycles or salt hydration) is common in arid and coastal settings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which classification sometimes includes reduction and chelation as chemical weathering processes?
questions.explanation: Some school classifications also include reduction and chelation along with solution, carbonation, oxidation, hydration and hydrolysis.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between solution and carbonation?

options.A: Solution is direct dissolution; carbonation is an acid-assisted reaction involving CO2 and water
options.B: Solution involves oxygen; carbonation involves ice
options.C: Solution is physical; carbonation is biological

questions.explanation: Solution is direct dissolution of soluble minerals. Carbonation is a particular acid-assisted reaction involving CO2 and water, especially effective on calcite-rich limestone.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process produces calcium bicarbonate that is carried away in groundwater?
questions.explanation: Carbonation: carbonic acid reacts with calcite producing soluble calcium bicarbonate that is carried away in groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process is associated with karst topography?
questions.explanation: Carbonation is associated with karst features such as sinkholes, caves, caverns and underground drainage.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which two processes are often confused but differ in that one adds water to mineral structure and the other chemically alters minerals through reaction with water?
questions.explanation: Hydration adds water to a mineral structure; hydrolysis chemically alters minerals through reaction with water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of weathering changes mineral composition and may form clay?
questions.explanation: Chemical weathering changes mineral composition and may form new minerals such as clay.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which type of weathering increases exposed surface area and can accelerate chemical weathering?
questions.explanation: Physical weathering increases exposed surface area and can accelerate chemical weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is NOT a mechanism of physical weathering?
questions.explanation: Carbonation is a chemical weathering process, not a physical weathering mechanism.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is NOT a principal chemical weathering process named in the source?
questions.explanation: Exfoliation is a physical weathering effect (sheet peeling), not a chemical weathering process.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an example of biological weathering that is mechanical?
questions.explanation: Root wedging is a mechanical biological weathering process; lichen acids and microbial alteration are chemical.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an example of biological weathering that is chemical?
questions.explanation: Lichen acids dissolving minerals is a chemical biological weathering process; root wedging and burrowing are mechanical.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do burrowing animals contribute to weathering?
questions.explanation: Burrowing animals disturb and expose material, contributing to biological weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which human activities contribute to weathering?

options.A: Excavation, quarrying, mining, construction, ploughing and vegetation removal

questions.explanation: Human excavation, quarrying, mining, construction, ploughing and vegetation removal expose fresh rock or alter soil and water contact.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Lichens, bacteria and fungi can help initiate:
questions.explanation: Lichens, bacteria and fungi retain moisture and may release organic acids that dissolve or alter minerals, helping initiate soil formation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the role of organic acids released by roots and decaying plant matter?
questions.explanation: Roots and decaying plant matter can release organic acids that promote chemical alteration.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In the context of exfoliation, what varies with rock and setting?
questions.explanation: The dominant mechanism of exfoliation varies with rock and setting; thermal expansion, pressure release and sheet-joint development can all contribute.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process is NOT a chemical weathering process according to the source?
questions.explanation: Frost action is a physical weathering process, not a chemical one.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between weathering, erosion and mass wasting?

options.A: Weathering breaks down rock in place; erosion removes and transports material; mass wasting is downslope movement under gravity
options.B: Weathering transports material; erosion breaks it in place; mass wasting is chemical alteration
options.C: All three are the same process
options.D: Weathering and erosion are both in-situ processes

questions.explanation: Weathering breaks down rock in place; erosion removes and transports material; mass wasting is downslope movement of rock or soil under gravity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between regolith and soil?

options.A: Regolith is the loose weathered layer covering bedrock; soil is a biologically active part of regolith
options.B: Soil is unweathered bedrock; regolith is organic matter
options.D: Regolith is molten rock; soil is weathered rock

questions.explanation: Regolith is the loose, unconsolidated layer of weathered rock and mineral material covering bedrock. Soil is a biologically active part of regolith containing mineral particles, organic matter, water and air.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Soil development depends on which factors besides weathering?

options.A: Climate, organisms, relief, parent material and time

questions.explanation: Weathering supplies mineral material, but soil development also depends on climate, organisms, relief, parent material and time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is true about the three types of weathering?

options.A: They operate independently and never together
options.B: They often operate together rather than independently
options.C: Only one type operates at a time

questions.explanation: Physical, chemical and biological weathering often operate together rather than independently.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process is described as a 'sheet-peeling effect/result' rather than always a single independent process?
questions.explanation: Exfoliation is a sheet-peeling effect/result, not always a single independent process; unloading and thermal stress can contribute.

questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: Hydration is the chemical combination of water molecules with a mineral, often changing its structure and volume.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process involves the reaction between minerals and water in which ions are exchanged or removed and new minerals form?
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis is a reaction between minerals and water in which ions are exchanged or removed and new minerals form.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which process involves the direct dissolving of soluble minerals in water?
questions.explanation: Solution (dissolution) is the direct dissolving of soluble minerals in water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are stalactites and stalagmites formed by?

options.A: Precipitation of calcium carbonate from dripping water

questions.explanation: Stalactites and stalagmites form by precipitation of calcium carbonate from dripping water after dissolution and transport.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What does the term 'in-situ' mean in the context of weathering?

options.A: Material is transported far from its origin
options.B: Rock is broken down or chemically altered where it is located
options.C: Material is deposited in a new location

questions.explanation: In-situ means rock is broken down or chemically altered where it is located; the material generally remains at or near its place of origin.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an agent of erosion?
questions.explanation: Weathering is not an agent of erosion; it breaks down rock in place. Erosion involves removal and transportation by rivers, wind, glaciers, waves or other agents.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of mass wasting?

options.A: Downslope movement of rock or soil under gravity
options.C: Freezing and thawing of water in cracks

questions.explanation: Mass wasting is the downslope movement of rock or soil under gravity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: Regolith is the loose, unconsolidated layer of weathered rock and mineral material covering bedrock.

questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: Soil is a biologically active part of regolith containing mineral particles, organic matter, water and air.

options.B: Weathering supplies mineral material but soil development depends on other factors too

options.D: Soil formation does not require weathering

questions.explanation: Weathering supplies mineral material, but soil development also depends on climate, organisms, relief, parent material and time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.explanation: Longitude alone does not directly determine weathering. Climate, rock/mineral composition, rock structure, surface area, relief and drainage, vegetation and organisms, and time are the main controlling factors.

options.C: A type of chemical weathering process

questions.explanation: Regolith is the loose, unconsolidated layer of weathered rock and mineral material covering bedrock.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is soil in relation to regolith?

options.A: Soil is completely unrelated to regolith
options.B: Soil is a biologically active part of regolith containing mineral particles, organic matter, water and air
options.C: Soil is the same as bedrock
options.D: Soil is a type of mass wasting

questions.explanation: Soil is a biologically active part of regolith containing mineral particles, organic matter, water and air.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Does weathering always produce soil?

options.B: No, weathering supplies mineral material but soil development also depends on climate, organisms, relief, parent material and time
options.C: Yes, but only in tropical regions
options.D: No, weathering never contributes to soil formation

questions.explanation: Weathering supplies mineral material, but soil development also depends on climate, organisms, relief, parent material and time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the three broad types of weathering?
questions.explanation: The three broad types are physical (mechanical), chemical and biological weathering. They often operate together rather than independently.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is physical weathering?

options.A: Decomposition of rock through chemical reactions
options.B: Breakdown of rock into smaller fragments without significant change in chemical or mineral composition
options.C: Alteration of rock by living organisms
options.D: Transport of rock fragments by wind

questions.explanation: Physical weathering is the breakdown of rock into smaller fragments without significant change in chemical or mineral composition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What effect does physical weathering have on chemical weathering?

options.A: It slows down chemical weathering by reducing surface area
options.B: It increases exposed surface area and can accelerate chemical weathering
options.D: It has no effect on chemical weathering

questions.explanation: Physical weathering increases exposed surface area and can accelerate chemical weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main mechanisms of physical weathering?

options.B: Thermal expansion and contraction; frost action; pressure release and unloading; salt-crystal growth; wetting and drying; and mechanical abrasion
options.D: Root wedging and organic acid dissolution

questions.explanation: The main mechanisms of physical weathering are thermal expansion and contraction; frost action (freeze-thaw); pressure release and unloading; salt-crystal growth; wetting and drying; and mechanical abrasion. Exfoliation is a characteristic sheet-peeling effect.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does thermal weathering occur?

options.B: Repeated heating and cooling cause expansion and contraction; differential expansion among minerals creates stress, cracks and granular disintegration
options.C: Through the freezing of water in cracks
options.D: Through the growth of salt crystals in pores

questions.explanation: Thermal weathering occurs through repeated heating and cooling causing expansion and contraction. Differential expansion among minerals creates stress, cracks and granular disintegration. It can be important where daily temperature ranges are large.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is exfoliation?

options.A: The dissolving of calcite in acidic water
options.B: Peeling or separation of curved, concentric outer sheets or slabs from a rock mass, often resembling onion layers
options.C: The freezing and expansion of water in rock cracks
options.D: The chemical combination of water with a mineral

questions.explanation: Exfoliation is the peeling or separation of curved, concentric outer sheets or slabs from a rock mass, often resembling onion layers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Explain exfoliation by pressure release (unloading).

options.A: When overlying material is removed, pressure on formerly buried massive rock decreases; the rock expands slightly and sheet joints develop roughly parallel to the land surface; outer slabs may detach
options.B: Water freezes in cracks and expands by 9%
options.C: Saline water enters pores and evaporates
options.D: Iron-bearing minerals oxidise to iron oxides

questions.explanation: When overlying material is removed, pressure on formerly buried massive rock decreases. The rock expands slightly and sheet joints develop roughly parallel to the land surface; outer slabs may detach.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Is exfoliation caused only by heating and cooling?

options.A: Yes, thermal expansion is the only cause
options.B: No, pressure release and sheet-joint development are important explanations; the dominant mechanism varies with rock and setting
options.C: Yes, exfoliation is exclusively a chemical process
options.D: No, exfoliation is caused only by frost action

questions.explanation: Textbooks sometimes emphasise thermal expansion, but pressure release and sheet-joint development are important explanations. The dominant mechanism varies with rock and setting.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is frost action?

options.A: Water enters joints and cracks; on freezing it expands by about 9% in volume, exerting pressure on crack walls; repeated freeze-thaw cycles widen cracks and detach angular fragments
options.B: Saline water enters pores and crystallises
options.C: Iron minerals oxidise and weaken rock

questions.explanation: Frost action: water enters joints and cracks. On freezing it expands by about 9% in volume, exerting pressure on crack walls. Repeated freeze-thaw cycles widen cracks and detach angular fragments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where is frost action most effective?

options.B: Where temperatures repeatedly cross the freezing point and water is available, particularly high mountains and cold regions
options.D: In coastal areas with high salinity

questions.explanation: Frost action is most effective where temperatures repeatedly cross the freezing point and water is available, particularly high mountains and cold regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is salt weathering?

options.A: Saline water enters pores and cracks; crystal growth, crystallisation cycles or salt hydration exert pressure and disaggregate rock
options.B: Water freezes in cracks and expands
options.C: Iron minerals oxidise to form rust

questions.explanation: Salt weathering: saline water enters pores and cracks; crystal growth, crystallisation cycles or salt hydration exert pressure and disaggregate rock. It is common in arid and coastal settings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: In which environments is salt weathering common?
questions.explanation: Salt weathering is common in arid and coastal settings where saline water enters pores and evaporates.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do wetting and drying cause weathering?

options.A: Some clay-rich materials swell when wet and shrink when dry; repeated cycles create stress, cracks and weakening
options.B: Water freezes and expands in cracks

questions.explanation: Some clay-rich materials swell when wet and shrink when dry. Repeated cycles create stress, cracks and weakening.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is chemical weathering?

options.A: Breakdown of rock into smaller fragments without chemical change
options.B: Decomposition or alteration of rocks and minerals through reactions with water, dissolved substances, oxygen and atmospheric gases
options.C: Physical breaking of rock by plant roots
options.D: Transport of weathered material by rivers

questions.explanation: Chemical weathering is the decomposition or alteration of rocks and minerals through reactions with water, dissolved substances, oxygen and atmospheric gases. It changes mineral composition and may form new minerals such as clay.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which conditions favour chemical weathering?

options.B: Warmth, moisture, water circulation, reactive minerals, vegetation and a large exposed surface area

questions.explanation: Warmth, moisture, water circulation, reactive minerals, vegetation and a large exposed surface area generally accelerate chemical weathering. Rates also depend on drainage, acidity and rock composition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Name the principal chemical weathering processes.

options.A: Frost action, exfoliation and salt weathering
options.B: Solution, carbonation, oxidation, hydration and hydrolysis
options.C: Root wedging, abrasion and thermal expansion

questions.explanation: The principal chemical weathering processes are solution, carbonation, oxidation, hydration and hydrolysis. Some school classifications also include reduction and chelation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is solution (dissolution) in weathering?

options.A: Direct dissolving of soluble minerals in water
options.C: Chemical combination of water with a mineral
options.D: Reaction of water with minerals changing their composition

questions.explanation: Solution (dissolution) is the direct dissolving of soluble minerals in water. Halite and gypsum are examples; calcite can dissolve in acidic water, particularly water containing carbonic acid.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which minerals are examples of substances that dissolve directly in water?
questions.explanation: Halite and gypsum are examples of soluble minerals that dissolve directly in water. Calcite can dissolve in acidic water, particularly water containing carbonic acid.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is carbonation?

options.A: Carbon dioxide dissolves in water to form weak carbonic acid; this reacts with carbonate minerals, especially calcite in limestone, producing soluble calcium bicarbonate that is carried away in groundwater
options.B: Iron-bearing minerals oxidise to iron oxides
options.C: Water combines chemically with a mineral structure
options.D: Minerals react with water and form clay

questions.explanation: Carbonation: carbon dioxide dissolves in water to form weak carbonic acid. This reacts with carbonate minerals, especially calcite in limestone, producing soluble calcium bicarbonate that is carried away in groundwater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What landforms are associated with carbonation?

options.B: Karst features: enlarged joints and grikes, sinkholes/dolines, swallow holes, caves, caverns and underground drainage

questions.explanation: Landforms associated with carbonation include karst features: enlarged joints and grikes, sinkholes/dolines, swallow holes, caves, caverns and underground drainage. Stalactites and stalagmites form later by precipitation of calcium carbonate from dripping water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do stalactites and stalagmites form?

options.A: By freezing of water in caves
options.B: By precipitation of calcium carbonate from dripping water after dissolution and transport

questions.explanation: Stalactites and stalagmites form by precipitation of calcium carbonate from dripping water after dissolution and transport.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is oxidation in weathering?

options.A: A reaction involving oxygen/electron transfer; iron-bearing minerals commonly oxidise to iron oxides and hydroxides, producing red, yellow or brown staining and weakening rock
options.B: Direct dissolving of minerals in water
options.C: Chemical combination of water with a mineral
options.D: Reaction of water with minerals to form clay

questions.explanation: Oxidation is a reaction involving oxygen/electron transfer. Iron-bearing minerals commonly oxidise to iron oxides and hydroxides, producing red, yellow or brown staining and weakening rock.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Give examples of oxidation products in weathering.
questions.explanation: Iron-bearing minerals may weather to hematite and goethite, which commonly impart red, yellow or brown colours.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is hydration in weathering?

options.A: Chemical combination of water molecules with a mineral, often changing its structure and volume
options.B: Direct dissolving of minerals in water
options.D: Reaction of water with minerals changing their composition

questions.explanation: Hydration is the chemical combination of water molecules with a mineral, often changing its structure and volume. An example is anhydrite (CaSO4) hydrating to gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an example of hydration?
questions.explanation: Anhydrite (CaSO4) hydrating to gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) is an example of hydration, which incorporates water into a mineral structure.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Differentiate hydration and hydrolysis.

options.A: Hydration incorporates water into a mineral structure; hydrolysis involves reaction of water (often H+ or OH-) with a mineral, changing its composition
options.B: Hydration involves oxygen; hydrolysis involves carbon dioxide
options.C: Hydration dissolves minerals; hydrolysis freezes water

questions.explanation: Hydration incorporates water into a mineral structure. Hydrolysis involves reaction of water (often H+ or OH-) with a mineral, changing its composition; feldspar can alter to clay minerals.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is hydrolysis?

options.A: Reaction between minerals and water in which ions are exchanged or removed and new minerals form
options.B: Direct dissolving of minerals in water
options.C: Chemical combination of water with a mineral structure

questions.explanation: Hydrolysis is a reaction between minerals and water in which ions are exchanged or removed and new minerals form. Feldspar may be transformed into kaolinite or other clay minerals, releasing dissolved ions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Feldspar commonly alters to clay minerals through which process?
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis changes feldspar composition and can form clay minerals such as kaolinite.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is carbonation important in limestone regions?

options.A: Limestone is rich in quartz which dissolves easily
options.B: Limestone is rich in calcite, which reacts with weak carbonic acid; dissolution along joints creates underground drainage and karst topography
options.C: Limestone contains iron which oxidises rapidly
options.D: Limestone is resistant to all chemical weathering

questions.explanation: Limestone is rich in calcite, which reacts with weak carbonic acid. Dissolution along joints creates underground drainage and karst topography.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is biological weathering?

options.A: Physical breakdown or chemical alteration of rock caused by living organisms and their activities
options.B: Breakdown of rock by temperature changes
options.C: Dissolution of rock by carbonic acid
options.D: Transport of weathered material by organisms

questions.explanation: Biological weathering is the physical breakdown or chemical alteration of rock caused by living organisms and their activities.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do plants cause weathering?

options.A: Roots enter cracks and grow, exerting pressure that widens them; roots and decaying plant matter can also release organic acids that promote chemical alteration
options.B: Plants absorb all water from rocks
options.C: Plants prevent any weathering from occurring

questions.explanation: Roots enter cracks and grow, exerting pressure that widens them. Roots and decaying plant matter can also release organic acids that promote chemical alteration.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do lichens and microorganisms weather rocks?

options.B: They retain moisture and may release organic acids or other compounds that dissolve or alter minerals; they can help initiate soil formation
options.C: They prevent weathering by covering the rock surface
options.D: They only grow on already weathered rock

questions.explanation: Lichens, bacteria and fungi retain moisture and may release organic acids or other compounds that dissolve or alter minerals. They can help initiate soil formation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do animals and humans contribute to weathering?

options.A: Burrowing animals disturb and expose material; human excavation, quarrying, mining, construction, ploughing and vegetation removal expose fresh rock or alter soil and water contact
options.B: They have no effect on weathering
options.D: They prevent weathering by stabilising rock

questions.explanation: Burrowing animals disturb and expose material. Human excavation, quarrying, mining, construction, ploughing and vegetation removal expose fresh rock or alter soil and water contact.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Is biological weathering only physical?

options.A: Yes, biological weathering is always mechanical
options.B: No, root wedging is mechanical while organic-acid reactions and microbial alteration are chemical; biological weathering includes both
options.C: Yes, biological weathering is always chemical
options.D: No, biological weathering never involves chemical processes

questions.explanation: Biological weathering includes both mechanical processes (such as root wedging) and chemical processes (such as organic-acid reactions and microbial alteration).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main controlling factors of weathering?

options.A: Climate; rock/mineral composition; rock structure; surface area; relief and drainage; vegetation and organisms; and time

questions.explanation: The main controlling factors are climate; rock/mineral composition; rock structure; surface area; relief and drainage; vegetation and organisms; and time.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does climate control weathering?

options.A: Temperature and rainfall control freeze-thaw, thermal stress, water availability and chemical reaction rates; warm, wet climates generally favour chemical weathering; cold climates favour frost action where freeze-thaw cycles occur; arid settings often favour physical and salt weathering
options.B: Climate has no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Temperature and rainfall control freeze-thaw, thermal stress, water availability and chemical reaction rates. Warm, wet climates generally favour chemical weathering; cold climates favour frost action where freeze-thaw cycles occur; arid settings often favour physical and salt weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does rock/mineral composition control weathering?

options.A: Minerals differ in resistance; quartz is relatively resistant to chemical weathering; many feldspars and ferromagnesian minerals alter more readily; calcite is susceptible to weakly acidic water; texture and cementation also matter
options.B: All minerals weather at the same rate
options.D: Composition has no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Minerals differ in resistance. Quartz is relatively resistant to chemical weathering; many feldspars and ferromagnesian minerals alter more readily; calcite is susceptible to weakly acidic water. Texture and cementation also matter.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does rock structure control weathering?

options.A: Joints, bedding planes, faults, fractures and cleavage provide pathways for water, air and roots; closely jointed rocks expose more surfaces to weathering
options.B: Rock structure has no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Joints, bedding planes, faults, fractures and cleavage provide pathways for water, air and roots. Closely jointed rocks expose more surfaces to weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does surface area affect weathering?

options.A: Small fragments have a larger surface-area-to-volume ratio than one large block of equal mass and generally weather faster
options.B: Surface area has no effect on weathering
options.C: Larger blocks weather faster than small fragments
options.D: Surface area only affects chemical weathering

questions.explanation: Small fragments have a larger surface-area-to-volume ratio than one large block of equal mass and generally weather faster.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do relief, slope and drainage affect weathering?

options.A: Slope affects water residence time, runoff and removal of weathered material; drainage controls the circulation of fresh water and oxygen and the chemical conditions within rock and soil
options.B: Relief and drainage have no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Slope affects water residence time, runoff and removal of weathered material. Drainage controls the circulation of fresh water and oxygen and the chemical conditions within rock and soil.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does vegetation and organisms affect weathering?

options.A: Roots, soil organisms, organic acids and decaying litter influence moisture, acidity and mechanical stress; vegetation may protect the surface while promoting weathering below it
options.B: Vegetation has no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Roots, soil organisms, organic acids and decaying litter influence moisture, acidity and mechanical stress. Vegetation may protect the surface while promoting weathering below it.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does time affect weathering?

options.A: Longer exposure generally allows more weathering if conditions remain favourable and material is not removed; age alone does not determine the degree of weathering
options.B: Time has no effect on weathering
options.D: Age alone determines the degree of weathering

questions.explanation: Longer exposure generally allows more weathering if conditions remain favourable and material is not removed. Age alone does not determine the degree of weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why does a warm, humid climate favour chemical weathering?

options.A: Water supports dissolution and chemical reactions, while higher temperatures generally accelerate reaction rates; soil CO2 and organic acids can further increase the chemical activity of water
options.C: Chemical weathering only occurs in cold climates

questions.explanation: Water supports dissolution and chemical reactions, while higher temperatures generally accelerate reaction rates. Soil CO2 and organic acids can further increase the chemical activity of water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why can the same rock weather differently in different climates?

options.A: Water availability, temperature range, freeze-thaw frequency, vegetation, drainage and exposure differ, changing both the dominant process and its rate
options.D: Climate has no effect on weathering

questions.explanation: Water availability, temperature range, freeze-thaw frequency, vegetation, drainage and exposure differ, changing both the dominant process and its rate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main effect of physical weathering?

options.C: Organisms cause physical and/or chemical change

questions.explanation: The main effect of physical weathering is breaking rock into fragments. There is little or no chemical change in composition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main effect of chemical weathering?
questions.explanation: The main effect of chemical weathering is changing mineral composition. It may form new minerals such as clay.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main effect of biological weathering?

options.C: Organisms cause physical and/or chemical change

questions.explanation: Biological weathering involves organisms causing physical and/or chemical change. It may or may not change composition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the agents of physical weathering?
questions.explanation: The agents of physical weathering are temperature, ice, salts and pressure.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the agents of chemical weathering?
questions.explanation: The agents of chemical weathering are water, oxygen, CO2 and acids.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the agents of biological weathering?
questions.explanation: The agents of biological weathering are roots, lichens, microbes and animals.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an example of physical weathering?
questions.explanation: Frost action and exfoliation are examples of physical weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an example of chemical weathering?
questions.explanation: Oxidation, carbonation and solution are examples of chemical weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is an example of biological weathering?
questions.explanation: Root wedging and lichen acids are examples of biological weathering.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key mechanism of exfoliation?

options.A: Curved outer sheets peel off; commonly linked to unloading/sheet joints
options.B: Water freezes and expands in cracks

questions.explanation: Exfoliation results in curved outer sheets peeling off; it is commonly linked to unloading/sheet joints.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where does frost action occur in India?

options.B: High Himalayan and other high-altitude environments where water repeatedly freezes and thaws

questions.explanation: Frost action occurs in high Himalayan and other high-altitude environments where water repeatedly freezes and thaws.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where in India is carbonation/karst weathering prominent?

options.B: Limestone terrains in Meghalaya and other limestone belts

questions.explanation: Carbonation/karst weathering is prominent in limestone terrains in Meghalaya and other limestone belts. World examples include the Dinaric Karst and Guilin region of China.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where are exfoliation and sheet joints found in India?

options.B: Massive granitic terrains, including parts of the Indian Peninsular uplands; exfoliation domes also occur in granitic landscapes worldwide

questions.explanation: Exfoliation and sheet joints occur in massive granitic terrains, including parts of the Indian Peninsular uplands. Exfoliation domes also occur in granitic landscapes worldwide.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where is oxidation weathering prominent in India?

options.A: Iron-rich rocks and lateritic weathering profiles in tropical and subtropical regions

questions.explanation: Oxidation is prominent in iron-rich rocks and lateritic weathering profiles in tropical and subtropical regions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where is salt weathering common?

options.B: Arid and coastal environments where saline water enters pores and evaporates

questions.explanation: Salt weathering is common in arid and coastal environments where saline water enters pores and evaporates.

questions.explanation: Weathering is in situ; erosion involves removal and transport.

questions.explanation: Exfoliation is a sheet-peeling effect/result, not always a single independent process; unloading and thermal stress can contribute.

questions.explanation: Weathering is the breakdown or alteration of rock in place (in situ).

options.A: Enlarged joints formed by carbonation dissolution

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are dolines?
questions.explanation: Dolines are sinkholes formed by limestone dissolution, a karst feature associated with carbonation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are swallow holes?

options.A: Points where surface water disappears underground in karst regions

questions.explanation: Swallow holes are points where surface water disappears underground in karst regions, associated with carbonation.

questions.question: What is a cavern in karst topography?

options.A: A large underground cave formed by limestone dissolution
